title: Who did better when the matches were not equal?
description: In a second series one batter played five matches and the other played four. The board shares each total equally over its matches to get the mean, and then compares the two means. Keeko doubts that the bigger total must mean the better batter.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the number of matches differs, compare the means, not the totals. Watch for students who compare the two totals and ignore how many matches each batter played.

source: In the second series Shubman scored 23, 7, 10, 52 and 18 in
video_script.why: The child can add the runs but has not seen why unequal numbers of matches make a total unfair to compare.
video_script.substitution: The mean, the total shared equally over the matches, replaces the total when the match counts differ.
video_script.anchor: A table of runs in a second series, five matches for one batter and four for the other
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred and ten is more than ninety six
video_script.wrong_move: compares totals although the numbers of matches differ

final_answer.value: Ziva, with a mean of 24 runs per match against 22
final_answer.spoken: the second batter, with a mean of twenty four runs per match against twenty two

names.Leeza: batter who plays five matches in the second series
names.Ziva: batter who plays four matches in the second series

maths_rules: second batter: 26, 53, 2, 15 in 4 matches, one match not played
110 / 5 = 22 runs per match; 96 / 4 = 24 runs per match
video_script.design: A table with five match columns, where the second row has a blank column. Each total is shared equally into its own columns, and the two shares are compared.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a table with five match columns, a full row for one batter and a row with one blank column for the other

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the table of five matches slides in
marks.m3: the blank column in the second row blinks
marks.m4: a question mark rises beside the table

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a table from your book, for another cricket series.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Leeza played five matches in this series.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ziva did not play one of the matches.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Who do you think performed better in this series?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of runs is poured into one heap and dealt out equally across its match columns; the equal share is labelled mean (average)

marks.g1: the runs of one row slide into one heap
marks.g2: the heap is dealt out equally across the match columns
marks.g3: the equal share is labelled mean

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A total alone is not fair when the number of matches is different.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>We share the total equally over the matches played.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The equal share is called the mean, or the average.

beats.on_screen: Given: Leeza scored 23, 7, 10, 52, 18 in 5 matches; Ziva scored 26, 53, 2, 15 in 4 matches

marks.given: the two rows of runs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Leeza scored twenty three, seven, ten, fifty two and eighteen in five matches.
Ziva scored twenty six, fifty three, two and fifteen in four matches.

beats.on_screen: To find: who performed better on average

marks.find: the words on average are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find who performed better on average.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, totals: 23 + 7 + 10 + 52 + 18 = 110 runs in 5 matches; 26 + 53 + 2 + 15 = 96 runs in 4 matches

marks.s1: the first row is added to its total
marks.s1b: the first row of runs is highlighted
marks.s2: the second row is added to its total
marks.s3: the numbers of matches, 5 and 4, are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add the runs of each batter to get the total.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Leeza has twenty three plus seven plus ten plus fifty two plus eighteen.
That makes one hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Ziva has twenty six plus fifty three plus two plus fifteen, which is ninety six.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>The totals come from five matches and four matches, so they do not compare fairly.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, mean = total ÷ number of matches: Leeza 110 ÷ 5 = 22 runs per match

marks.d1: the rule mean = total ÷ number of matches is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, the mean is the total divided by the number of matches.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>For Leeza, one hundred and ten divided by five gives twenty two runs per match.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, mean = total ÷ number of matches: Ziva 96 ÷ 4 = 24 runs per match

marks.c2: the result 24 is boxed beside the result 22

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, do the same for Ziva.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Ninety six divided by four gives twenty four runs per match.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, compare the means: 24 is more than 22

marks.e1: the two means sit side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>Step four, compare the two means.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Twenty four is more than twenty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Ziva, with a mean of 24 runs per match against 22
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ziva performed better on average.
The mean is twenty four runs per match against twenty two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble shows 110 is more than 96 with a tick; the fifth match of the first row glows; the tick is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble with 110 more than 96 and a tick appears
marks.fix: the fifth match column glows in the first row

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Leeza did better, because one hundred and ten is more than ninety six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But Leeza had one extra match in which to score runs.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>Comparing totals is not fair when the number of matches is different.
